entityName: DLR - INSTITUTE FOR THE PROTECTION OF TERRESTRIAL INFRASTRUCTES (DLR PI AN)
entityDescription:
The Institute for the Protection of Terrestrial Infrastructures (PI) has been dedicated since its foundation in 2019 to theprotection and security of critical infrastructures on earth. We develop concepts, processes and technologies that strengthen and improve the resilience of organisations and systems. In this, we focus on people, technology and the system as a whole.
Modern societies depend on the unrestricted availability of their critical infrastructures. Protecting them from dangers is essential for prosperity and social stability.Critical infrastructuresare, for example, water and energy supply, rail and air transport, hospitals, public authorities, fire brigade and disaster control facilities or hazardous materials storage facilities. In that sense, infrastructures are systems, processes and resources that in their entirety provide for the supply of society.
Crime, terrorist attacks and the effects of natural disasters and pandemics as well as cybercrime arereal dangersthat threaten the security of societies. The more complex and interconnected societies and their infrastructures are, the more vulnerable they are to threats. As a key tool for responding to threats and improving the resilience of infrastructures, we apply theconcept of the Digital Twin.
Digital twins represent the closest possiblereplication of a real system. The virtual image is continuously updated by comparing it with real-time data. Based on this time-accurate virtual image, a variety ofanalyses and forecastson the behaviour of the real system can be carried out and visualised. In this way, all parties involved can gain a deeper understanding of the respective infrastructure and initiate the influencing of the real system with the help of suitableactuators or decisions.
In order to detect imminent dangers at an early stage,intelligent sensors are far superior to human senses in certain situations. We develop sensor technologies for different purposes and create methods for evaluating sensor observations.
Using methods of prediction, simulation of scenarios, operational resilience management and decision support, operators and emergency forces are supported in the best possible way to get ahead of the situation, i.e. to anticipate the negative development of the situation.
In our view, the concept of the Digital Twin is the key to realising a resilience cycle. This enables us to assess and continuously improve the resilience of the infrastructure under consideration in almost any situation:
- By continuously monitoring the infrastructures, disruptions and triggers of cascading effects can already be detected as soon as a crisis situation occurs and operational measures to protect the infrastructurecan be initiated.
- During a crisis, the concept of the Digital Twin of the real infrastructure allows us to understand the situation and adapt to the dangers and threats.
- After a crisis, we can use the data and models to simulate threats and impacts on the threatened systems.
- Based on these findings, we analyse the trajectories and can derive the necessary optimisation of the infrastructure.

entityDescription: PASI is a startup company whose main objective is the democratization of expertise and education in the field of human spaceflight. PASI provides human spaceflight consulting services to public, private, and defense organizations through specialized consultants. Personnel involved in the proposed study: Laura André-Boyet has 16 years of experience in the Human Spaceflight industry. She worked for Medes as a Space Physiology Experiment Manager at the Centre National d'Etudes Spatiales (National Center for Space Studies, CNES) in Toulouse, France. She works in the training division of the European Astronaut Center (EAC) in Cologne, Germany, as an Astronaut Instructor and Simulations Director at the service of the European Space Agency (ESA). In 2018, she founded the Professional Association of Space Instructors® (PASI), where she works as a parabolic flight instructor and as a human spaceflight expert consultant for public, private, and defense organizations. She regularly participates in many collaborative research projects, mainly focused on physiology in extreme environments and space analogues.Finally, within the framework of national defence, she graduated in 2022 from the Cycle d'Etudes Stratégiques de la Marine and joined the operational reserve of the French Air Force the same year as a Lieutenant-Colonel expert in space operations.

entityDescription: HyImpulse is a New-Space start-up based in Hardthausen, Germany. We are developing a mini launcher using disruptive technologies to provide low-cost small-sat launch opportunities for Europe and the whole world. HyImpulse was founded by 5 DLR employees with excellent experience in chemical and hybrid rocket propulsion as well as a good network in the international space industry. We are sure that disruptive technologies and ways of thinking can lower the cost of orbital launches and at the same time increase flexibility for our customers. These disruptions include in the first place inherently safe hybrid rocket propulsion systems with advanced paraffin-based fuels. Our launcher therefore will use "green propulsion"​ without toxicity and environmental harms. Other important disruptive technologies include COTS components for avionics, state of the art production technology for light weight composite structures, 3D printing of various parts, and decreasing cost by serial production. For example, our main engine will be used several times on the launcher. Our first product in development is a single stage sounding rocket using a hybrid rocket engine to deliver institutional and commercial experiments into a micro gravity environment during a suborbital flight. Based on that technology demonstrator, a mini launcher with a target payload of 400 kg into a Low Earth Orbit will be developed.

Ikkaido is an NGO with Special Consultative Status to the United Nations, working in the field of diversity and inclusion for youth, women and girls and all persons with fewer opportunities, especially persons with a disability in sport, education, empowerment, employment and entrepreneurship.
 
A Registered Charity, Ikkaido is a signature to the Marseilles Declaration on Inclusion and the Geneva Convention 190 for the elimination of violence and harassment in the world of work, with an additional focus on domestic violence and gender-based violence against women.
 
Based in the multi-cultural City of Oxford, Ikkaido works with disadvantaged communities; NEETs, and young people with fewer opportunities, especially those with a disability and mental health issues, to help them tackle their issues and motivate them towards taking steps towards better health, recovery and engagement in the community. Ikkaido has grown participation in sport and physical activity for over 7500 disabled and disadvantaged young people. Most of the participants are NEET receiving some form of benefit support. The main centre of operation is in Stoke Mandeville Stadium; the birthplace of the Paralympics with resultant connections and working relationships with Paralympic, Olympic and Special Olympic federations all around the world.
 
Ikkaido is a Recognised VET Centre of Education and is regulated by OFQUAL. They are experts in inclusion and the development, writing and delivery of accredited inclusive qualifications.Ikkaido builds qualifications with inclusion theory at the core, allowing any participant to achieve. Ikkaido has established inclusive qualifications at levels 1 through 6 in the field of coaching and education for youth with fewer opportunities, youth workers, coaches, teaching assistants and teachers nationally, in Europe and internationally. Elearning and blended learning are used and reinforced by non-formal learning.
 
Ikkaido has MoUs with many martial arts federations and associations around the world to create Ikkaido Inclusive Festivals of Martial Arts providing participation for persons with a disability.
 
Ikkaido has provided keynote addresses on inclusion including in both Japan and Korea at the World Congress of The Association For International Sport for All (TAFISA), the World Festival of Martial Arts in Russia, the World Martial Arts Games in London, the World Kickboxing Championship in Germany, the Fudokan World Championships and the International Conference of Inclusive Sport in Portugal.
 
The Ikkaido board is inclusive and contains 80% disabled and 20% non-disabled people and maintains gender balance. All Ikkaido staff are persons with disabilities and fewer opportunities.

entityDescription:
Nuremberg Institute of Technology, or Nuremberg Tech for short, is one of Germany’s largest universities,with over 13,000 students.
The university is a corporation under public law with the right to self-govern within the framework of legislation, while also being a State institution. In accordance with Article 2 of the Bavarian State Universities Act, the universities for applied sciences provide application-based teaching in order to deliver education that enables students to apply scientific methods and use creative activities independently in professional practice. Within the scope of the existing infrastructure, universities of applied sciences are able to undertakeapplication-oriented research and development projects, if predominantly third-party funding is available.

The university’s roots (history) can be traced back to the year 1823 and the founding of the Städtische Polytechnikum (Municipal Polytechnic) – the oldest of our forerunners. The university is named after the world-renowned physicist, Georg Simon Ohm (biography), who was a physics and mathematics professor in Nuremberg between 1833 and 1849, and also fulfilled the role of rector. 
Innovative technological developments shape our living environment today and will do so tomorrow. A systematic transfer of research outcomes strengthens the innovative ability of small and medium-sized enterprises. As one of Germany’s universities with the largest amount of third-party funding, Nuremberg Tech exerts an important influence on structural policy within the Nuremberg Metropolitan Region. 
The aim is to continue developing this collaboration with regional, national, and international partners. Together, the engineering Faculties at Nuremberg Tech operate over 150 laboratories, which represent a high degree of innovative potential to find solutions to the key issues facing our society and our business sector.

The Arsakeio comprises six schools, with campuses in Psychiko [Attica], Ekali (Tosítseio campus) [Attica], Thessaloniki, Patras, Ioannina, and also Tirana, Albania. Arsakeio has several Departments and Services. The pedagogical system and the curricula are supervised by the Supervisor (Επόπτης) aided by a board of Coordinators. Each Coordinator overviews and guides the educators of a set of subjects (i.e. languages, physics, maths, informatics, etc.). There are three FL departments (English, French, German). The Counseling Services (psychologists and career counselors) have offices on all campuses and run relevant programs. The Cultural Programs Service organizes various cultural events, educational programs and guided tours to museums and archaeological sites for the students. In Arsakeio there are a Junior Achievement - Young Enterprise Europe Group, and active groups of robotics, STEM, and F1 in Schools. The Arsakeio digital Program Department runs and supports the digital school e-arsakeioTM. Arsakeia schools at Patra organize yearly a MUN conference (ATS MUN). The Supervisor and her assisting board organize every year a two-day student conference, Arts and Letters Contests, day-conferences and competitions on Mathematics and Physics, meanwhile the Arsakeio's students participate in various European programs (Erasmus+, Forensics, European Youth Parliament, etc.) and in national and international competitions (F1 in Schools, MUNs, Olympiads of Physics and Mathematics).

description:
Instituto Pedro Nunes (IPN) is a non-profit private organization which promotes innovation and the transfer of technology, establishing the interface between business and academia. Created in 1991 through an initiative of the University of Coimbra, IPN has currently a team of almost 100 permanent staff to support start-ups and researchers in these activities. IPN operates in three complementary areas: 
1. Incubation and acceleration of technology-based enterprises activities. IPN help start-ups with technical guidance in the establishment and early stages of business development, tutorial follow-up for developing business plans, support for attracting investment and securing funding, intellectual property and legal assistance (e.g. technology transfer contracts and the registration of patents or trademarks), access to and contact with various national and international research centres, knowledge institutions and sources of funding. 
2. Research and technological development. IPN’s technological infrastructure includes a set of six laboratories in diversified technological areas which, along with its established connections with higher education institutions, R&TD organisations and both national and international companies, place IPN in a privileged position for jointly conducting R&TD activities with enterprises. IPN is thus able to provide multidisciplinary support for product creation and innovative processes within an entrepreneurial environment. This includes technological development, access to sources of funding and assistance with intellectual property queries and entry to international markets.
 3. Highly specialized training.

Since 2014, Instituto Pedro Nunes leads the first European Space Solutions Centre, among the other 21 ESA centers across Europe, hosting within the same entity the three areas promoting downstream businesses: ESA Business Incubation Centre, ESA Technology Brokers and ESA Business Applications Ambassadors Platform (AP). ESA Space Solutions Portugal has the support of ESA - European Space Agency, Portugal Space - Portuguese Space Agency and ANACOM, along with a wide range of stakeholders such as incubators, universities and regional authorities, amongst others.
